issues.description: Fast-path regex may skip unitless `0` time values that the original code processed
issues.detail: CSS allows `0` (without unit) in time-valued properties like `transition-duration: 0`. The regex `/\dm?s/i` requires a trailing `s`, so a value of `0` is now skipped entirely. If the original valueParser path reported unitless zero as below the minimum, this is a behavior change. Worth confirming with a test case.

issues.description: Regex `/\dm?s/i` can false-positive on non-time tokens, reducing fast-path effectiveness
issues.detail: Patterns like `#1ms` in a hex-ish identifier, or `1s` appearing inside an unrelated function name, would defeat the early exit. Correctness is preserved (slow path still runs), but the optimization yields less than expected when declarations contain incidental matches. Anchoring to a word boundary (e.g. `/\d(?:ms|s)\b/i`) would tighten it.

issues.description: No new test exercises the early-return path
issues.detail: The changeset advertises a perf fix but the diff adds no test confirming that declarations without time values are skipped, nor that edge cases (`0`, `0s`, `var(--d)`, `calc(1s*2)`, uppercase `MS`) still behave correctly. A targeted test would lock in the new contract and guard against regressions.

issues.description: Move of `propertyName` assignment is fine but loses a micro-skip opportunity
issues.detail: The fast-path filters on value content but still walks every declaration. Since the rule only applies to a known set of time-valued properties, an earlier check on `decl.prop` (cheap string compare) before any regex test could skip even more work. Optional; the current change already addresses the hot path.

review.summary: The PR adds a cheap regex pre-filter to skip expensive value parsing when a declaration's value contains no time-like token. The optimization is correct in spirit and preserves the slow-path for any matching value, but `/\dm?s/i` would skip unitless `0` (a legal CSS time value), which is a potential behavior change worth verifying. Suggest tightening the regex with a word boundary, adding tests for edge cases (`0`, uppercase `MS`, `var()`, `calc()`), and confirming `0` semantics with the existing rule behavior.
